text:
ajay: seeing a write fanout spike on local-ssd pool in us-east1 — GPU attaches are being held (attach-queue +120s). alerting now.

ajay: metric snapshot: iops_p95=420k, write_amp=3.2, janitor_queue_len=450

sre-bot: [ALERT] local-nvme iops surge in us-east1 (pool: scratch-us-east1-a). triggered at 2026-03-23T14:12:17Z. linked runbook: https://runbooks/redwood/scratch-iops-surge

maria: which cohort? is this new after the scrub deploy last night? :eyes:

ajay: looks like cohort v2 (recent scrub tuning). scrub cadence overlapped with a batch job backfill, causing big small-write storms. happened ~14:08UTC.

jonathan: can we throttle the scruber temporarily? last time we did `janitor.rate_limit=50r/s` and it helped.

elaine: cost question — if we keep holds and push users to dedicated, what's delta? rough estimate: 6h of queued attach = ~12k in lost throughput, but dedicated shift adds ~$2k/day if we move long-term. short-term tradeoff probably cheaper to throttle.

ajay: agree. proposing quick remediation: 1) throttle janitor to 30r/s in affected zone 2) disable spot auto-scale up for 10m to avoid more attaches 3) kick a fast rebalance to spread hot files.

maria: ok runbook patch please. also add a metric alert for janitor_queue_len > 300 to avoid next time.

jonathan: patch (one-liner):
```bash
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/janitor JANITOR_RATE=30 --overwrite
sh /opt/ops/decider disable-autoscale --pool scratch-us-east1-a --duration 10m
```

ajay: executing now. will post iostat after changes. :thumbsup:

ajay: iostat -x after throttle (snippet):
```
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rsec/s wsec/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1: 0.00 0.00 50.00 12000.00 400.00 420000.00 800 84000 16.5 1.21 0.10 0.15 1.05 0.98 82.1
```

ajay: queue len dropped from 450 -> 65 in 3m. attach backlog processing resumed.

elaine: nice. any risk of data loss from throttling?

jonathan: throttling safe — janitor will slow tombstone sweeps only; we keep full correctness. risk is longer retention of temp files but acceptable.

maria: can we add an automated fallback to route new attaches to dedicated pool if janitor_queue_len > 300 for >2m? saves manual toggles.

ajay: noted — raising a ticket for routing policy change. for now I left autoscale disabled and increased attach workers from 2->4 to catch up.

ajay: follow-up numbers: attach latency median down from 95s -> 12s, GPU attach rate normalizing.

ajay: re-enabled autoscale (10m elapsed). will monitor 15m. thanks all. :raised_hands:

maria: add postmortem note and cost comparison in handbook, assigning to @jonathan to draft.

jonathan: on it, will include timeline, root cause (scrub + batch backfill overlap), mitigations, and a queued alert.

sre-bot: Incident closed by ajay at 2026-03-23T14:20:30Z. summary: janitor rate lowered, autoscale paused briefly, attach workers increased.

ajay: thumbs up — closing thread.
